# Referral / intake coordinator

Draft role definition owned by Alamo Workflow. Inferred role split; confirm duties and ownership with staff. This is not an employee assignment or permission grant.

## Purpose

Turn an incoming referral and its documents into a correctly identified, attributable intake record with missing requirements and the next owner visible.

## Scope

Authorized referral queue and assigned intake resources; identity matching or visibility never assigns clinical responsibility.

## Applications

- Pipeline
- Alamo Workflow

## Working rhythm

- At intake: establish identity, source and packet inventory.
- During queue review: follow unresolved requests and reconcile new documents.
- At transfer: record the next responsible owner and outstanding requirements.

## Knowledge and learning

- Person versus referral versus stay identity
- Original document, extraction and reviewed fact
- Requirements and assignment states
- Upload/save recovery and private document handling

## Workflow summaries

- Receive and orient a referral: New referral or reopened intake
- Track missing intake information: Missing packet item or newly received evidence

## Knowledge objects

- referral
- person-reference
- evidence-document
- requirement
- assignment

## Proposed measures

- Time from received referral to recorded intake owner, when both timestamps exist
- Missing-requirement age and unresolved identity exceptions; unknown coverage remains explicit

## Questions for staff review

- Is intake a dedicated job or shared with assessors/coordinators?
- Who may resolve duplicate identities and merge or link records?
- Which requirements are mandatory by referral source and facility?
